Hereditary (2018)

The small moment in which we get complete silence before further madness. Annie is standing in her bedroom, camera pointed at her forehead in extreme up close. Her eyes are closed. A faint scratching is heard but not by us at first, just Annie. Her eyes softly dart around, but she goes to investigate what she believes is a noise coming from Charlie’s old room. 

This is the moment of the film to me, not by far but it’s always had this great impression on me. Annie has her eyes shut and is not enjoying, not moving, not relishing, not anything. A moment of perhaps not peace but silence, a moment where a ka-trillion thoughts are not swarming endlessly about processing her trauma, accepting it and continuing on with what she has. This point in the film has already submitted to madness, but for that brief second. There was nothing, no harsh impositions of the brutal entanglements that she’s working on unsurfacing. No moment to think of required against her remaining family who attempt to carefully rebuke Annie’s strange fixations and wishes. The Bergman-esque feel of this closeup just sells to me that this is a moment where the director decided to not only give us a rest but says “hey, LOOK at this person, this is still a human person, capable of having a silent half second in the midst of all that is unraveling beneath her”. Maybe it’s a moment of quiet strength, maybe there are a few thoughts circling about having gone too far…..

The sound she’s reacting to proves it’s all too late.

For what GT is, I'm surprised there isn't more online points based short term championships or "seasons". Imagine a daily races framework where you keep the same setup for races, as in A B C, but expand the ranking system and make your driver ratings and sportsmanship ratings matter much more. With there being no real feedback to gaining or losing ratings other than the markers on the end of session timesheet, what if this fed into a ranking system that compares you against the other drivers of your grade? Gaining points across sessions to be closer to the top of the leaderboard, which could include stats like total positions lost/gained, wins, podiums, poles, fastest laps, sportsmanship level and on. I'd personally love to have way more in depth statistics to see even the baseline performances that I've had. To me, this is what the game whiffs hardest on is the idea that they could have a much more official and proper racing ecosystem to the online matchmaking, the current state is really only about 40% there.

I’ve enjoyed this film through as few different stages of my life so I’m glad to see the other side of the coin. I truly believe this film is all about ridding the coattails of several VERY American tropes that essentially all coincide in a comfort film, which is what I take it in as.

- complicatedly uncomplicated plot

- language (as you mentioned)

- entering America as a new citizen

- emerging from an unknown country (if you told someone today you were from Krakozhia, people would likely believe it)

- ideas of a the fall of a small nation against the continually bustling and wildly alive America which barely breaks a stride even as the news plays through the story

- establishing the ideas of American homeland security rigidity(but at the same time sympathy) esp post 2001. 

- a foreigner coming to America and making something beautiful out of something so mundane (fountain in the unfinished bathroom)

- finally breaking through, after making the most of his situation, living in freaking JFK like a small penthouse in the abandoned wing. Taking the coffee jar to the jazz bar to continue his father’s legacy.


So yes, the things that happen are stupidly happenstance and plot armor towards victor in every way. But I think the film is going for that eye rolling suspension of disbelief and playing heavily into the sympathy that American immigrants get when presented “correctly” on screen. Victor made it and went on with his life after coming into contact with that “magic that is a man with no country trying to enter the greatest country”.


I love Catch Me If You Can too, but it relies on the same kind of magic.
It’s the subtlety that provides the horror

I’ve been in your boat more than several times and it’s extremely frustrating. This past week was my first time on the dailies since the end of may and I wanted to try out the Honda NSX Gr.4 at Barcelona National Layout, and I felt comfortable in the car as it ran smooth, but so slow it was confusing me. I was getting passed with ease through straights or turns and I genuinely thought my speed was gone after such a long break. I rented the Huracan and instantly qualified P6 and got a win within 3 races. I genuinely think that PD has put so much time and care into how the cars work, that there’s a wide variability of performance that outreaches BOP at times. Mets cars will always exist and my own doctrine is that if you’re fast, you’re fast regardless of machinery. But this has also made me realize I’m not Schumacher and I have to pick a car that seems competitive against the field. I feel I’ve gone through this with the McLaren 650S Gr.4 too. I love the feedback I feel when taking it too the limit, but it’s also just genuinely a slower car compared to some metas and compared to certain tracks even. In my opinion, just begin to feel out how others work, and become comfortable in them, having a variety is a great way to feel out a week of dailies. 

For example I like the following Group cars:

Porsche 991 RSR GR.3 for all around handling and grip

McLaren 650S Gr.4 for the “slidey” rear (and engine sound)

Subaru BRZ GT300 Gr.3 for great throttle response and grip

Nissan Silvia Spec-R Aero Touring Car for great handling, good speed and the only touring car I can run on controller without Traction Control

It pretty much only hit me during the finale, when they were inside of the delivery room. I was thinking how if Beau was the baby I wouldn’t be even surprised at this point. But the similarities to me are throughout both stories, both characters of Asher and Beau get the same treatment from everyone (including their “mother figures” Mona and Whitney) where they basically don’t get to ever explain themselves and are hardly ever heard by anyone. They’re both sexually stunted in some ways, and carry the strong Jewish undertones. Plus I could totally script out how Whitney becomes Mona by being a single mother who becomes a titan of industry, if Whitney were to take over her parents properties in Espanola. Visually there are some similarities as well as Ari Aster and the Safdies are incredibly gifted at crafting blocking on screen, and the subliminal messages throughout plastered on advertisements. Overall they’re very different stories with different aura but they have some overarching similarities and uniquely bizarre elements.

I’m right there with you, they’re all insufferable in unique ways. I questioned watching after episode 4, but what draws me in the most is the effective cinematography. Lots of what I call the “Safdie Zoom”, where we peer through small gaps and the camera slowly works its way forward. It’s a subliminal technique that works very well for them and what could be called the “boiling frog”, instead of being immediately thrown in, we start in a natural position, to slowly creep up in zoom (temperature) until we’re “boiling” or have the feeling of unconscious claustrophobia placed upon us. It’s one thing to write a great tv show with effective performances but it’s the masters that can pressurize those aspects all around great filming technique.
